description: Original synthetic test footage for Frame scene navigation. Exact edit ground truth, not a benchmark for real camera footage.

fixtures.expected: Four distinct shots. Check suggested boundaries near 4, 8, and 12 seconds; enter each section and inspect its first and last frames.

One uninterrupted moving shot. Time-based sections must remain useful without inventing scene changes. The final section must reach the final source frame. Low resolution tests timeline duration, not 4K decoder stress.
One shot with a continuous pan, one white frame at 5 seconds, and two black frames at 11 seconds. These flashes should not create persistent scene suggestions.

A fade-through-black transition spans 4–7 seconds, then a same-palette composition cut at 12 seconds. A coarse hard-cut detector may miss these; time sections and manual scrubbing must remain available. Black is intentional content, not proof of decode failure.

Ten shots, some only 0.1–0.3 seconds long. Coarse sampling can miss these; never create zero-length or overlapping sections or imply every cut was detected. A requested 0.75-second edit is quantized to the next 30 fps frame (0.7667 seconds).
Portrait source with real 15/30/60 fps timestamp intervals. Scene times remain source-relative. Frame numbers are approximate in Frame's current rate model; do not claim exact VFR frame stepping.
Twelve frames. Loading must finish, one usable section must cover the whole file, endpoint scrubbing must stay finite, and export must still work.

A short full-resolution 4K source with one cut at 2 seconds. Exported uncropped stills should remain 3840×2160. Simple synthetic imagery and a short duration do not reproduce sustained phone-footage decoder load.
